groups.sentence: Instructors check which tools students use contain AI and state in the syllabus whether grammar checkers, Grammarly and similar embedded tools are allowed.
Instructors give students specific guidance on which embedded or everyday tools are acceptable and help them recognize when AI is involved.
Students must not use AI writing assistants or editing tools such as Grammarly, Quillbot, and Wordtune in coursework.
Students do not use embedded, built-in, or plug-in AI tools for core assignments or to generate or heavily change text.
Students may use incidental or embedded tools, such as autocomplete, search features, and code completion, without disclosure or penalty.
Students turn off or restrict AI features when a ban applies, and confirm and limit what data AI tools can access.
AI agents and browser plugins can act on students' behalf, such as answering quizzes and discussion posts.
AI features are built into many common tools and applications, often without clear labeling.
Autonomous AI agents are prohibited, and agentic AI used to complete assessments without human interaction is cheating.
Administrators may block or disable AI tools, such as plugins and companion tools, on managed machines.
